title: Nightcore Maker – Speed Up Any Song Online Free
description: Free nightcore maker: turn any song into a nightcore or sped-up version in your browser with speed and pitch presets, then export MP3 or WAV. No signup, files stay on you
heroText: Turn any song into a nightcore version in your browser: faster, higher-pitched, brighter. Load a file from your device, apply the Nightcore preset or set speed and pitch yourself, hear the change live, and export the result as MP3 or WAV. Free, no signup, no watermark.

sections.title: The nightcore tool is on this screen
sections.body: This page is a working nightcore maker, not a description of one: it opens with the Nightcore preset already applied. Load a file and the waveform appears in the second deck.

items.title: Nightcore preset
items.body: One press sets 1.25x speed, +4 semitones of pitch and a light 12% reverb, which is the nightcore recipe most edits use: faster, higher and a little brighter without smearing the vocal.

items.title: Sped up version, your way
items.body: Prefer a mild lift for a reel or the full 1.5x for an energetic edit? Move speed across 0.5x to 1.5x and pitch across 12 semitones each way; the pitch field adds to the lift the speed itself gives the track. Play preview follows each change so you hear the result before rendering.

items.title: Daycore, the opposite direction
items.body: The same console slows a track down and lowers its pitch: Daycore is 0.75x with -5 semitones, 40% reverb and +4 dB bass. Both styles come from one workflow, and the same export.

items.title: Trim before export
items.body: The waveform shows the whole file with the trim marks on it. Set trim start and trim end in seconds, press Reset trim to start over, and the render contains exactly that section of the song.

sections.title: How to make a nightcore track here
sections.body: Nightcore is tempo and pitch raised together, and this tool handles both live in the browser through the [Web Audio API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Audio_API). Nothing is uploaded to a server on the way.

steps.title: Load the song
steps.body: Drag in an MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, FLAC or AAC file, or press Choose file. It decodes on your machine and draws its waveform; Try the sample loads a short built-in tone if you want to hear the preset first.

steps.title: Apply the preset or adjust by hand
steps.body: Nightcore is already selected on this page. Moving speed changes tempo and pitch together, tape-style, so a small speed lift already makes the track higher; the pitch field then adds whole semitones on top of that lift. Add a little reverb or bass if the result feels thin, and use trim start and trim end to keep the chorus you actually want.

steps.title: Export MP3 or WAV
steps.body: Render runs the same graph offline and reports the source length and the finished length before the download. Choose WAV for a 16-bit file or MP3 at 192 kbps, then press Download; it lands in your device's downloads folder, never on a server.

sections.title: Nightcore, daycore and slowed and reverb
sections.body: All three styles come from the same two numbers, speed and pitch. What changes is the direction and how far you push them. Each row is a style the presets on this page reach: press one, then move the sliders along that range.

items.title: Which one should you make?
items.body: Nightcore suits upbeat edits and dance clips; slowed and reverb suits chill and late-night moods. [The slowed vs nightcore comparison](/slowed-vs-nightcore/) works through when each one lands.

sections.title: Nightcore FAQ
sections.body: Answers to the questions visitors ask before their first sped-up export.

faq.question: What does a nightcore maker do to a song?
faq.answer: It raises playback speed and pitch together, which is what defines the style: the track gets faster, higher and brighter while staying recognizable. This page opens with that already set (1.25x, +4 semitones, 12% reverb), previews it live, then renders the result to WAV or MP3.

faq.question: Is nightcore the same as a sped up version?
faq.answer: Not quite. A plain sped-up version raises tempo while leaving pitch roughly where it was, so the vocal keeps its depth; nightcore lifts both. This engine moves the two together tape-style, so a milder lift is a smaller speed change — around 1.05x to 1.10x with pitch left at 0 — and pulling the pitch field down toward −2 st takes part of that lift back out.

faq.question: How much should I speed a song up for nightcore?
faq.answer: Most edits sit between 1.2x and 1.3x, and the preset lands at 1.25x. Past about 1.4x vocals start to sound thin and lyrics get hard to follow. Load a track and press Play preview after each step, and trust your ears over any fixed number.

faq.question: Does the nightcore maker cost anything or need an account?
faq.answer: No. It is free with no signup, no quota and no watermark. The audio decodes in your browser, so nothing installs and no file leaves your device; you can render as many WAV or MP3 files as you like.

faq.question: Can I make slowed and reverb or daycore here too?
faq.answer: Yes. Press Daycore for 0.75x speed, -5 semitones, 40% reverb and +4 dB bass, or press Classic Slowed + Reverb for 0.80x with 55% reverb. The [slowed and reverb guide](/how-to-make-slowed-and-reverb/) walks through each setting in order.

faq.question: Can I put nightcore edits on YouTube or TikTok?
faq.answer: The exported file plays anywhere, but publishing a derivative of a commercial recording is a rights decision only you can make. This tool processes your file locally and grants no copyright clearance, so check that you hold the rights before you post.
